title_en: Agriculture Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of consolidating and strengthening the basic position of agriculture in the national economy, deepening rural reform, developing agricultural productive forces, promoting agricultural modernization, safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations, increasing farmers' income, improving farmers' scientific and cultural quality, promoting the sustained, stable and healthy development of agriculture and the rural economy, and achieving the goal of building a well-off society in an all-round way.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "agriculture" means crop farming, forestry, animal husbandry and fishery and other industries, including the services directly related to the pre-production, in-production and post-production.
For the purposes of this Law, "agricultural production and operation organizations" mean rural collective economic organizations, specialized farmers' cooperative economic organizations, agricultural enterprises and other organizations engaged in agricultural production and operation.

Article 3 The State shall give priority to agriculture in the development of the national economy.
The basic objectives for the development of agriculture and the rural economy are: to establish a rural economic system that meets the requirements of the development of the socialist market economy, to constantly emancipate and develop the rural productive forces, to improve the overall quality and efficiency of agriculture, to ensure the supply and quality of agricultural products, to meet the needs of national economic development, population growth and improvement of living standards, to raise the income and living standards of farmers, to promote the transfer of surplus rural labor to non-agricultural industries and cities and towns, to narrow the gap between urban and rural areas and between regions, to build a rich, democratic and civilized new socialist countryside, and gradually to realize agricultural and rural modernization.

Article 4 The State shall take measures to ensure that agriculture plays a better role in providing food, industrial raw materials and other agricultural products, in maintaining and improving the ecological environment, and in promoting rural economic and social development and in other aspects.

Article 5 The State shall uphold and improve the basic economic system under which public ownership is the mainstay and diverse forms of ownership develop together, and revitalize the rural economy.
The State shall stabilize over the long term the two-tier management system in the countryside that combines centralized operations with decentralized operations on the basis of household contract management, develop the socialized service system, expand the strength of the collective economy, and guide farmers onto the path of common prosperity.
The State shall uphold and improve in the countryside the distribution system under which distribution according to work is the mainstay and multiple forms of distribution coexist.

Article 6 The State shall adhere to the policy of revitalizing agriculture through science, technology and education and the sustainable development of agriculture.
The State shall take measures to strengthen the construction of agricultural and rural infrastructure, adjust and optimize the agricultural and rural economic structure, promote industrialized operation of agriculture, develop agricultural science, technology and education, protect the agricultural ecological environment, promote agricultural mechanization and informatization, and improve the comprehensive agricultural production capacity.

Article 7 The State shall protect the property and other legitimate rights and interests of farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations from infringement.
The people's governments at all levels and the relevant departments thereof shall take measures to increase farmers' income and effectively lighten the burden on farmers.

Article 8 The whole society shall attach great importance to agriculture and support the development of agriculture.
The State shall give awards to units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in developing agriculture and the rural economy.

Article 9 The people's governments at all levels shall have unified responsibility for the work of agricultural and rural economic development, and shall organize the relevant departments and the whole society to do a good job in developing agriculture and in all work serving the development of agriculture.
The competent agricultural administrative department of the State Council shall be in charge of the work of agricultural and rural economic development nationwide, and the competent forestry administrative department of the State Council and other relevant departments shall, within the scope of their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the relevant work of agricultural and rural economic development.
The competent agricultural administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the work of agricultural and rural economic development, including crop farming, animal husbandry and fishery, within their respective administrative areas, and the competent forestry administrative departments shall be responsible for the forestry work within their respective administrative areas. The other relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within the scope of their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the relevant work serving agricultural production and operation within their respective administrative areas.

Article 10 The State shall practice the system of rural land contract operation, guarantee the long-term stability of rural land contract relations according to law, and protect farmers' right to use contracted land.
The methods, duration, rights and obligations of the party granting the contract and the party contracting the land, the protection and transfer of the right to contracted land operation, etc., shall be governed by the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Rural Land Contracts.
Rural collective economic organizations shall, on the basis of household contract operation, manage collective assets according to law, provide their members with services such as production, technology and information, organize the rational development and utilization of collective resources, and strengthen their economic strength.

Article 11 The State shall encourage farmers to voluntarily form various types of specialized cooperative economic organizations on the basis of household contract operation.
Specialized farmers' cooperative economic organizations shall adhere to the purpose of serving their members, and shall, in accordance with the principles of voluntary membership, freedom of withdrawal, democratic management and return of surplus, carry out agricultural production, operation and service activities within the scope prescribed by their articles of association according to law.
Specialized farmers' cooperative economic organizations may take various forms and shall be established and registered according to law. No organization or individual may infringe upon the property and operational autonomy of specialized farmers' cooperative economic organizations.

Article 12 Farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations may, on a voluntary basis, in accordance with the principle of combining democratic management, distribution according to work and distribution based on shares, make capital contributions in the form of funds, technology, physical objects, etc., and establish various types of enterprises according to law.

Article 13 The State shall take measures to develop multiple forms of industrialized operation of agriculture, and encourage and support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to develop integrated operation of production, processing and marketing.
The State shall guide and support enterprises, research institutions and other organizations engaged in the production, processing and circulation services of agricultural products, through entering into contracts with farmers or specialized farmers' cooperative economic organizations or establishing various types of enterprises, to form a community of shared interests and shared risks, to promote the industrialized operation of agriculture and to drive agricultural development.

Article 14 Farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations may, in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, establish various trade associations for agricultural products, to provide members with services such as production, marketing, information, technology and training, to play a coordinating and self-disciplinary role, to apply for trade remedy measures for agricultural products, and to safeguard the interests of members and the industry.

Article 15 The people's governments at or above the county level shall formulate agricultural development plans in accordance with the medium- and long-term plans for national economic and social development, the basic objectives of agricultural and rural economic development, and the regional planning of agricultural resources.
The competent agricultural administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall, in accordance with the agricultural development plans, take measures to give play to regional advantages, promote the formation of a rational regional distribution of agricultural production, and guide and coordinate the adjustment of agricultural and rural economic structure.

Article 16 The State shall guide and support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to, in light of local conditions and according to market demand, adjust and optimize the agricultural production structure, coordinate the development of crop farming, forestry, animal husbandry and fishery, develop high-quality, high-yield and high-efficiency agriculture, and enhance the international competitiveness of agricultural products.
Crop farming shall take the optimization of varieties, the improvement of quality and the increase of benefits as the core, and adjust the crop structure, variety structure and quality structure.
Forestry ecological construction shall be strengthened, projects for the protection of natural forests, returning farmland to forests and the prevention and control of desertification shall be implemented, the construction of shelterbelt systems shall be strengthened, and the development of fast-growing and high-yielding timber forests, industrial raw material forests and fuel forests shall be accelerated.
Grassland protection and construction shall be strengthened, the development of animal husbandry shall be accelerated, pen feeding and shed feeding shall be promoted, the breeds of livestock and poultry shall be improved, and the feed industry and the livestock and poultry product processing industry shall be actively developed.
Fishery production shall protect and rationally utilize fishery resources, adjust the fishing structure, and actively develop aquaculture, deep-sea fisheries and aquatic product processing industry.
The people's governments at or above the county level shall formulate policies, allocate funds, and guide and support the adjustment of the agricultural structure.

Article 17 The people's governments at all levels shall take measures to strengthen comprehensive agricultural development and the construction of agricultural and rural infrastructure, including farmland water conservancy, protection of the agricultural ecological environment, rural roads, rural energy and power grids, storage and circulation of agricultural products, fishing ports, grassland fences, and bases for original seeds and improved varieties of animals and plants, so as to improve agricultural production conditions and protect and enhance the comprehensive agricultural production capacity.

Article 18 The State shall support the selection and breeding, production, renewal and popularization and use of improved varieties of animals and plants, encourage the combination of variety selection and breeding with production and operation, and implement the seed project and the improved variety project for livestock and poultry. The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall set up special funds for supporting the selection and breeding and popularization of improved varieties of animals and plants.

Article 19 The people's governments at all levels and agricultural production and operation organizations shall strengthen the construction of farmland water conservancy facilities, establish and improve the management system for farmland water conservancy facilities, conserve water, develop water-saving agriculture, strictly control, in accordance with law, the occupation of irrigation water sources by non-agricultural construction, and prohibit any organization or individual from illegally occupying or damaging farmland water conservancy facilities.
The State shall give priority support to water-deficient areas in developing water-saving agriculture.

Article 20 The State shall encourage and support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to use advanced and applicable agricultural machinery, strengthen the safety management of agricultural machinery, and raise the level of agricultural mechanization.
The State shall give support to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations in purchasing advanced agricultural machinery.

Article 21 People's governments at all levels shall support the development of meteorological services for agriculture, and improve the monitoring and forecasting capabilities of meteorological disasters.

Article 22 The State shall take measures to improve the quality of agricultural products, establish and improve the quality standard system for agricultural products and the quality inspection, testing and supervision system, and organize the production and operation of agricultural products in accordance with relevant technical specifications, operational procedures and quality, hygiene and safety standards to ensure the quality and safety of agricultural products.

Article 23 The State supports the establishment and improvement of a certification and labeling system for high-quality agricultural products according to law.
The State encourages and supports the development of high-quality agricultural production. Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in light of local conditions, take measures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State to develop high-quality agricultural production.
High-quality agricultural products that meet the standards set by the State may apply to use relevant marks in accordance with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Agricultural products that meet the requirements of designated places of origin and production standards may apply to use geographical indications for agricultural products in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws or administrative regulations.

Article 24 The State shall implement a system of animal and plant epidemic prevention and quarantine, improve the animal and plant epidemic prevention and quarantine system, strengthen the monitoring, early warning and control of animal epidemics and plant diseases, pests, weeds and rodents, establish a rapid eradication mechanism for major animal epidemics and plant diseases and pests, build animal disease-free zones, and implement plant protection projects.

Article 25 The production and operation of agricultural means of production such as pesticides, veterinary drugs, feed and feed additives, fertilizers, seeds, and agricultural machinery that may endanger the safety of humans and livestock shall be subject to a registration or licensing system in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
People's governments at all levels shall establish and improve a safe use system for agricultural means of production. Farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations shall not use agricultural means of production such as pesticides, veterinary drugs, feed additives and other prohibited products that are explicitly eliminated or prohibited by the State.
Producers and sellers of agricultural means of production shall be responsible for the quality of the products they produce and sell. It shall be prohibited to pass off inferior products as high-quality ones, counterfeit products as genuine ones, or unqualified products as qualified ones; it shall be prohibited to produce and sell agricultural means of production such as pesticides, veterinary drugs, feed additives, and agricultural machinery that are explicitly eliminated by the State.

Article 26 The purchase and sale of agricultural products shall be subject to market regulation. The State shall exercise necessary macro-control over the purchase and sale activities of major agricultural products that are vital to the national economy and the people's livelihood, establish a central and local graded reserve and regulation system, and improve the warehousing and transportation system to ensure supply and stabilize the market.

Article 27 The State shall gradually establish a unified, open, competitive and orderly market system for agricultural products, and formulate development plans for agricultural products wholesale markets. The State shall provide support to rural collective economic organizations and specialized farmer cooperative economic organizations in establishing agricultural products wholesale markets and agricultural products fair trade markets.
The administrative departments for industry and commerce and other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, manage agricultural products wholesale markets according to law, regulate trading order, and prevent local protectionism and unfair competition.

Article 28 The State encourages and supports the development of various forms of agricultural product circulation activities. It supports farmers and specialized farmer cooperative economic organizations in engaging in the purchase, wholesale, storage, transportation, retail and intermediary activities of agricultural products in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. It encourages supply and marketing cooperatives and other agricultural production and operation organizations engaged in the purchase and sale of agricultural products to provide market information, open up agricultural product circulation channels, and serve the sale of agricultural products.
People's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to urge relevant departments to ensure smooth transportation of agricultural products and reduce circulation costs. Relevant administrative departments shall simplify procedures to facilitate the transportation of fresh and live agricultural products. Unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, they shall not seize the means of transport for fresh and live agricultural products.

Article 29 The State supports the development of agricultural product processing industry and food industry to increase the added value of agricultural products. People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate development plans for agricultural product processing industry and food industry, guide agricultural product processing enterprises to form a reasonable regional layout and scale structure, and support specialized farmer cooperative economic organizations and township enterprises in engaging in agricultural product processing and comprehensive development and utilization.
The State shall establish and improve quality standards for processed agricultural products, perfect testing methods, and strengthen quality safety management and supervision during the processing of agricultural products to ensure food safety.

Article 30 The State encourages the development of import and export trade of agricultural products.
The State shall take measures such as strengthening international market research, providing information and marketing services to promote the export of agricultural products.
In order to maintain the order of agricultural product production and marketing and fair trade, an early warning system for agricultural product imports shall be established. When certain imported agricultural products have caused or are likely to cause a significant adverse impact on the production of relevant domestic agricultural products, the State may take necessary measures.

Article 31 The State shall take measures to protect and enhance the comprehensive grain production capacity, steadily raise the level of grain production, and ensure food security.
The State shall establish a farmland protection system and implement special protection for basic farmland according to law.

Article 32 The State shall give priority support to major grain-producing areas in terms of policies, funds, technology, etc., build stable commercial grain production bases, improve grain harvesting, storage and processing facilities, and raise the level of grain production, processing and economic benefits in major grain-producing areas.
The State supports the establishment of stable purchase and sale cooperation relationships between major grain-producing areas and major grain-marketing areas.

Article 33 When the market price of grain is too low, the State Council may decide to implement a protection price system for certain grain varieties. The protection price shall be determined in accordance with the principle of protecting farmers' interests and stabilizing grain production.
When farmers sell grain under the protection price system, the purchasing units entrusted by the State shall not refuse to purchase.
People's governments at or above the county level shall organize finance, banking and other departments as well as purchasing units entrusted by the State to raise sufficient grain purchase funds in a timely manner. No department, unit or individual may withhold or misappropriate such funds.

Article 34 The State shall establish an early warning system for food security and take measures to ensure grain supply. The State Council shall formulate grain security assurance targets and grain reserve quantity indicators, and organize relevant competent departments to conduct verification of farmland and grain stockpiles as necessary.
The State shall implement a central and local graded reserve and regulation system for grain, and build a warehousing and transportation system. Enterprises undertaking the task of state grain reserves shall ensure the quantity and quality of reserve grain in accordance with the provisions of the State.
Article 35 The State shall establish a grain risk fund to support grain reserves, stabilize the grain market and protect farmers' interests.
Article 36 The State advocates the cherishing and conservation of grain, and takes measures to improve the nutritional structure of the people's food.

Article 37 The State shall establish and improve the agricultural support and protection system, and adopt measures such as financial input, tax preferences and financial support to support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations in developing agricultural production and raising farmers' income levels in terms of capital input, scientific research and technology extension, education and training, supply of agricultural means of production, market information, quality standards, inspection and quarantine, socialized services, and disaster relief.
Without conflicting with the relevant international treaties concluded or acceded to by China, the State shall implement income support policies for farmers. The specific measures shall be formulated by the State Council.

Article 38 The State shall gradually increase the overall level of agricultural input. The annual growth rate of total agricultural input by the central finance and the finance of people's governments at or above the county level shall be higher than the growth rate of their regular fiscal revenue.
The funds allocated for agriculture in the fiscal budgets of people's governments at all levels shall be mainly used for: strengthening agricultural infrastructure construction; supporting agricultural restructuring, promoting industrialized operation of agriculture; protecting comprehensive grain production capacity, ensuring national food security; improving the animal and plant quarantine and epidemic prevention system, strengthening the prevention and control of animal epidemics and plant diseases, pests, weeds and rodents; establishing and improving the quality standards for agricultural products and the inspection, testing and supervision system, the agricultural products market and information service system; supporting agricultural scientific research and education, agricultural technology extension and farmer training; strengthening the construction of agricultural ecological environment protection; supporting the development of poverty-stricken areas; safeguarding farmers' income levels, etc.
The agricultural capital construction input for crop farming, forestry, animal husbandry, fishery, and farmland water conservancy by the finance at or above the county level shall be planned comprehensively and increased in a coordinated manner.
In order to accelerate the development of the western region, the State shall increase input for agricultural development and ecological environment protection in the western region.

Article 39 The funds allocated for agriculture in the annual fiscal budgets of people's governments at or above the county level shall be disbursed in full and on a timely basis. People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the supervision and management of the allocation and use of various state agricultural funds to ensure the safety of funds and improve the efficiency of fund utilization.
No unit or individual may withhold or misappropriate the fiscal funds and credit funds used for agriculture. Audit institutions shall, according to law, strengthen the audit supervision over the fiscal and credit funds used for agriculture.

Article 40 The State shall use tax, price, credit and other means to encourage and guide farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to increase input in agricultural production and operation and investment in capital construction such as small-scale farmland water conservancy.
The State encourages and supports farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to raise agricultural funds in various forms on a voluntary basis and according to law.

Article 41 The State shall encourage social funds to be invested in agriculture, and encourage enterprises, institutions, social organizations and individuals to donate money to establish various agricultural construction and agricultural science, technology and education funds.
The State shall take measures to promote the expanded utilization of foreign capital in agriculture.

Article 42 People's governments at all levels shall encourage and support enterprises, institutions and other types of economic organizations to provide agricultural information services.
The agricultural administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level and other relevant departments shall establish systems for collection, collation and dissemination of agricultural information, and promptly provide market information and other services to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations.

Article 43 The State shall encourage and support the development of agricultural industry.
The State shall adopt measures such as taxation and credit to encourage and support the production and trade of agricultural means of production, providing material guarantee for the stable growth of agricultural production.
The State shall adopt macro-control measures to maintain a reasonable parity between major agricultural means of production such as chemical fertilizers, pesticides, agricultural films, agricultural machinery and agricultural diesel and agricultural products.

Article 44 The State shall encourage supply and marketing cooperatives, rural collective economic organizations, specialized farmer cooperative economic organizations, other organizations and individuals to develop various forms of socialized services before, during and after agricultural production. People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall take measures to support the socialized agricultural service undertakings.
For those engaged in trans-regional agricultural socialized services, the relevant departments of agriculture, industry and commerce administration, transportation, public security, etc. shall take measures to provide support.

Article 45 The State shall establish and improve the rural financial system, strengthen the construction of rural credit system, and strengthen rural financial supervision.
Relevant financial institutions shall take measures to increase credit input, improve rural financial services, and provide credit support to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations in their agricultural production and operation activities.
Rural credit cooperatives shall adhere to the purpose of serving agriculture, farmers and rural economic development, and shall give priority to providing credit services to local farmers in their production and operation activities.
The State shall, through measures such as interest subsidies, encourage financial institutions to provide loans to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations for their agricultural production and operation activities.

Article 46 The State shall establish and improve the agricultural insurance system.
The State shall gradually establish and improve the policy-based agricultural insurance system. It shall encourage and support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to establish mutual and cooperative insurance organizations serving agricultural production and operation activities, and encourage commercial insurance companies to carry out agricultural insurance business.
Agricultural insurance shall follow the principle of voluntariness. No organization or individual may compel farmers or agricultural production and operation organizations to participate in agricultural insurance.

Article 47 People's governments at all levels shall take measures to improve the capability of agriculture to defend against natural disasters, do a good job in disaster prevention, resistance and relief, help disaster victims restore production, organize production self-help, and carry out social mutual assistance and relief; provide relief and support to disaster victims who lack basic living guarantees.

Article 48 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall formulate plans for the development of agricultural science and technology and agricultural education, and develop agricultural science, technology and education undertakings.
People's governments at or above the county level shall gradually increase funds for agricultural science and technology and agricultural education in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
The State shall encourage and attract enterprises and other social forces to increase investment in agricultural science and technology, and encourage farmers, agricultural production and operation organizations, enterprises and institutions, etc. to run agricultural science, technology and education undertakings according to law.

Article 49 The State shall protect intellectual property such as new plant varieties and geographical indications of agricultural products, encourage and guide agricultural research and education institutions to strengthen basic research and applied research in agricultural science and technology, disseminate and popularize agricultural science and technology knowledge, accelerate the transformation and industrialization of scientific and technological achievements, and promote progress in agricultural science and technology.
The relevant departments of the State Council shall organize scientific and technological research on major key technologies in agriculture. The State shall take measures to promote international cooperation and exchanges in agricultural science, technology and education, and encourage the introduction of advanced foreign technologies.

Article 50 The State shall support the cause of agricultural technology extension, establish an agricultural technology extension system that combines government support with market guidance, paid services with free services, and state agricultural technology extension institutions with social forces, so as to promote the prompt application of advanced agricultural technologies in agricultural production.

Article 51 Agricultural technology extension institutions established by the State shall rely on agricultural technology experiment and demonstration bases, undertake public welfare duties such as the extension and demonstration of key technologies needed for the public, and provide free agricultural technical services to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations.
People's governments at or above the county level shall, according to the needs of agricultural production development, stabilize and strengthen the agricultural technology extension team, and ensure the working funds of agricultural technology extension institutions.
People's governments at all levels shall take measures to guarantee and improve the working conditions, salaries and living conditions of professional scientific and technical personnel engaged in agricultural technology extension in accordance with the provisions of the State, and encourage them to serve agriculture.

Article 52 Agricultural research institutions, relevant schools, specialized farmer cooperatives, agriculture-related enterprises, mass science and technology organizations and relevant scientific and technical personnel may, according to the needs of farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations, provide free services, or provide paid services and obtain lawful income through forms such as technology transfer, technical services, technical contracting, technical consulting and technology as equity. Agricultural research institutions, relevant schools, specialized farmer cooperatives, agriculture-related enterprises, mass science and technology organizations and relevant scientific and technical personnel shall improve service levels and ensure service quality.
The State shall grant preferential treatment in taxation, credit, etc. to enterprises established by agricultural research institutions, relevant schools and agricultural technology extension institutions to serve agriculture.
The State shall encourage and support farmers, supply and marketing cooperatives, other enterprises and institutions, etc. to participate in agricultural technology extension work.

Article 53 The State shall establish a continuing education system for agricultural professional and technical personnel. The agricultural administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, together with the relevant departments such as education and personnel, formulate plans for continuing education of agricultural professional and technical personnel, and organize their implementation.

Article 54 The State shall implement compulsory education in rural areas according to law and guarantee the funds for compulsory education. The salaries of teaching and administrative staff of ordinary primary and secondary schools established by the State in rural areas shall be uniformly disbursed by the people's governments at the county level in accordance with the provisions of the State, and the funds for the construction and maintenance of teaching facilities such as school buildings shall be uniformly arranged by the people's governments at the county level in accordance with the provisions of the State.

Article 55 The State shall develop vocational education in agriculture. The relevant departments of the State Council shall, in accordance with the unified provisions of the national vocational qualification certificate system, carry out work on occupational classification and vocational skill appraisal in the agricultural industry, and manage the vocational qualification certificates in the agricultural industry.

Article 56 The State shall take measures to encourage farmers to adopt advanced agricultural technologies, support farmers in establishing various science and technology organizations, carry out training in practical agricultural techniques, farmer green certificate training and other employment training, so as to improve the cultural and technical quality of farmers.

Article 57 To develop agriculture and the rural economy, it is necessary to rationally utilize and protect natural resources such as land, water, forests, grasslands, wild animals and plants, rationally develop and utilize renewable energy and clean energy such as hydropower, biogas, solar energy and wind energy, develop eco-agriculture, and protect and improve the ecological environment.
People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate agricultural resource zoning or zoning for rational utilization and protection of agricultural resources, and establish a monitoring system for agricultural resources.

Article 58 Farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations shall maintain cultivated land, rationally use chemical fertilizers, pesticides and agricultural films, increase the use of organic fertilizers, adopt advanced technologies, protect and improve soil fertility, and prevent pollution, damage and fertility decline of agricultural land.
The agricultural administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to support farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations in strengthening the construction of cultivated land quality, and conduct regular monitoring of cultivated land quality.

Article 59 People's governments at all levels shall take measures to strengthen comprehensive control of small watersheds, and prevent and control soil erosion. Units and individuals engaged in production and construction activities that may cause soil erosion must take preventive measures and shall be responsible for controlling the soil erosion caused by such production and construction activities.
People's governments at all levels shall take measures to prevent land desertification and control desertified land. The State Council and the local people's governments at or above the county level in areas where desertified land is located shall formulate plans for desertification prevention and control in accordance with the provisions of law, and organize their implementation.

Article 60 The State shall implement a system of compulsory tree planting for all citizens. People's governments at all levels shall take measures to organize the masses to plant trees and afforest, protect forest land and trees, prevent forest fires, prevent and control forest pests and diseases, stop indiscriminate and illegal felling of trees, and increase the forest coverage rate.
The State shall implement a system of logging prohibition or logging limitation in natural forest protection areas, and strengthen afforestation and forest protection.

The relevant local people's governments shall strengthen the protection, construction and management of grasslands, guide and organize farmers (herdsmen) and agricultural (livestock) production and operation entities to construct artificial pastures, forage grass and feed bases and improve natural grasslands, implement the determination of livestock numbers based on grass yield, control the carrying capacity, promote the systems of rotational grazing, rest grazing and prohibition of grazing, protect grassland vegetation, and prevent grassland degradation, desertification and salinization.

It is prohibited to open up land by destroying forests and grasslands, to open up land by burning mountains, and to open up steep slopes where the state prohibits opening up. The land already opened up shall be gradually returned to forests and grasslands.
It is prohibited to reclaim land from lakes and to enclose for reclamation wetlands where the state prohibits enclosure. The land already enclosed shall be gradually returned to lakes and wetlands.
Farmers who carry out conversion of cropland within the scope of the plans approved by the State Council shall be granted subsidies in accordance with state regulations.

People's governments at all levels shall take measures to implement the systems of fishing quotas and prohibition of fishing and suspension of fishing according to law, increase fishery resources, and protect the ecological environment of fishing waters.
The state shall guide and support farmers (fishermen) and agricultural (fishery) production and operation entities engaged in the fishing industry to engage in aquaculture or other occupations. For farmers (fishermen) who shift production and change their occupation in accordance with the unified plans of the local people's governments, subsidies shall be granted in accordance with state regulations.

The state shall establish a system for the protection of biological species resources related to agricultural production, protect biodiversity, and implement key protection for rare, endangered and precious biological resources and their original habitats. The introduction of biological species resources from abroad shall be registered or approved according to law, and corresponding safety control measures shall be taken.
The research, experimentation, production, processing, operation and other applications of agricultural genetically modified organisms must strictly implement various safety control measures in accordance with state regulations.

The competent administrative departments for agriculture at all levels shall guide farmers and agricultural production and operation entities to adopt biological measures or use highly effective, low-toxicity, low-residue pesticides and veterinary drugs to prevent and control plant and animal diseases, pests, weeds and rodents.
The stalks and other residual materials after harvesting of agricultural products shall be comprehensively utilized and properly disposed of to prevent environmental pollution and ecological damage.
Units and individuals engaged in large-scale breeding of livestock and poultry and other animals shall conduct harmless treatment or comprehensive utilization of feces, wastewater and other wastes. Units and individuals engaged in aquaculture shall reasonably apply bait, fertilizers and drugs to prevent environmental pollution and ecological damage.

People's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to urge relevant units to carry out treatment and prevent pollution of the agricultural ecological environment by waste water, waste gas and solid waste. Where the discharge of waste water, waste gas or solid waste causes pollution accidents of the agricultural ecological environment, the competent administrative department for environmental protection or the competent administrative department for agriculture shall investigate and handle the matter according to law; if losses are caused to farmers or agricultural production and operation entities, the responsible parties shall compensate according to law.

Any organ or unit that collects administrative or institutional fees from farmers or agricultural production and operation entities must do so in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. The items, scope and standards of fees shall be published. For fees not based on laws or regulations, farmers and agricultural production and operation entities have the right to refuse.
Any organ or unit that imposes fines or penalties on farmers or agricultural production and operation entities must do so in accordance with the provisions of laws, regulations and rules. For fines not based on laws, regulations or rules, farmers and agricultural production and operation entities have the right to refuse.
No organ or unit may, in any manner, apportion expenses on farmers or agricultural production and operation entities. Unless otherwise provided by laws or regulations, any organ or unit that, in any manner, requires farmers or agricultural production and operation entities to provide human, financial or material resources constitutes an apportionment. Farmers and agricultural production and operation entities have the right to refuse any form of apportionment.

People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments and subordinate units may not, in any manner, raise funds from farmers or agricultural production and operation entities.
Without the basis of laws or regulations or without the approval of the State Council, no organ or unit may conduct any form of target achievement, upgrading or acceptance inspection activities in rural areas.

Farmers and agricultural production and operation entities shall bear the obligation to pay taxes in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations. The tax authorities and units that withhold or collect taxes shall levy taxes according to law, and may not illegally apportion taxes or levy taxes by other illegal means.

For compulsory education in rural areas, besides the fees charged in accordance with the regulations of the State Council, no other fees may be collected from farmers or students. No organ or unit may charge fees from farmers through rural primary and secondary schools.

When the state expropriates land owned by peasant collectives according to law, it shall protect the lawful rights and interests of farmers and rural collective economic organizations, grant expropriation compensation to farmers and rural collective economic organizations according to law, and no unit or individual may intercept or misappropriate the compensation fees for land expropriation.

People's governments at all levels, rural collective economic organizations or villagers committees may not, in the course of adjustment of agricultural and rural economic structure, industrialized operation of agriculture and transfer of the right to land contractual management, infringe upon farmers' right to land contractual management, interfere with the production and operation projects arranged independently by farmers, or compel farmers to purchase designated means of production or sell agricultural products through designated channels.

If a rural collective economic organization or a villagers committee needs to raise funds or collect labor from its members (villagers) for the development of production or the establishment of public welfare undertakings, it may only do so after it is approved by a majority vote of the members (villagers) meeting or the members (villagers) representative meeting.
When a rural collective economic organization or a villagers committee raises funds or collects labor in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it shall not exceed the upper limit control standards prescribed by the people's government at or above the provincial level, and it is prohibited to forcibly use money in lieu of labor.
Rural collective economic organizations and villagers committees shall disclose to the villagers important matters concerning the interests of the farmers, and regularly publish financial accounts to accept supervision by the farmers.

Any unit or individual that provides production, technology, information, culture, insurance or other paid services to farmers or agricultural production and operation entities must adhere to the principle of voluntariness, and may not compel farmers or agricultural production and operation entities to accept the services.

When purchasing agricultural products, the units purchasing agricultural products may not depress the grade or price, and may not deduct any fees from the price paid. If laws or administrative regulations provide for the withholding or collection of taxes, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
If a dispute arises between the unit purchasing agricultural products and the seller of agricultural products over the quality grade of the agricultural products, the dispute may be submitted to a legally qualified agricultural product quality inspection institution for testing.

Where a user of agricultural means of production suffers losses due to quality problems of the means of production, the operator who sold such means of production shall provide compensation, and the amount of compensation shall include the purchase price, relevant expenses and loss of obtainable benefits.

For the protection of their own lawful rights and interests, farmers or agricultural production and operation entities have the right to report the situation and raise lawful demands to people's governments at all levels and the relevant departments thereof. The people's governments and the relevant departments thereof shall give timely replies to the reasonable demands raised by farmers or agricultural production and operation entities in accordance with state regulations.

Where a violation of legal provisions infringes upon the rights and interests of farmers, farmers or agricultural production and operation entities may apply for administrative reconsideration or file a lawsuit with the People's Court according to law. The relevant people's governments and their relevant departments or the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.
The People's Court and the competent judicial administrative organs shall provide legal aid to farmers in accordance with the relevant provisions.

The state adheres to the policy of coordinated development of urban and rural areas, supports the development of the secondary and tertiary industries in rural areas, adjusts and optimizes the rural economic structure, increases farmers' income, promotes the comprehensive development of the rural economy, and gradually narrows the gap between urban and rural areas.

People's governments at all levels shall take measures to develop township enterprises, support the development of agriculture, and transfer surplus agricultural labor force.
The state shall improve the support measures for the development of township enterprises, guide township enterprises to optimize their structure, update their technology, and improve their quality.

Article 81 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the local economic development level, location advantages and resource conditions, and in accordance with the principles of rational distribution, scientific planning and land conservation, promote the construction of small rural towns with focus.
Local people's governments at all levels shall pay attention to utilizing market mechanisms, improve relevant policies, attract farmers and social funds to invest in the development and construction of small towns, develop the secondary and tertiary industries, and guide the relatively concentrated development of township enterprises.

Article 82 The State shall take measures to guide the rational and orderly flow of surplus rural labor between urban and rural areas and among regions. Local people's governments at all levels shall, according to law, protect the lawful rights and interests of rural labor entering cities and towns for employment, and shall not impose unreasonable restrictions; those already imposed shall be abolished.

Article 83 The State shall gradually improve the rural social relief system to ensure the basic livelihood of rural households enjoying the five guarantees, impoverished disabled farmers, impoverished elderly farmers and other farmers who have lost the ability to work.

Article 84 The State shall encourage and support farmers in consolidating and developing rural cooperative medical care and other forms of medical security, so as to improve the health level of farmers.

Article 85 The State shall support poverty-stricken areas in improving their economic development conditions and assist them in carrying out economic development. The people's governments at the provincial level shall, in accordance with the overall goals and requirements of the State for supporting poverty-stricken areas, formulate plans for poverty alleviation through development and organize their implementation.
People's governments at all levels shall adhere to the development-oriented poverty alleviation policy, organize farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations in poverty-stricken areas to use poverty alleviation funds rationally, rely on their own efforts to change the backward situation, and guide farmers in poverty-stricken areas to adjust their economic structure and develop local resources. Poverty alleviation through development shall be combined with resource protection and ecological construction to promote coordinated economic and social development and comprehensive progress in poverty-stricken areas.

Article 86 The central and provincial finance departments shall include the input for poverty alleviation through development in the annual fiscal budget, increase it year by year, and increase financial transfer payments and construction fund input to poverty-stricken areas.
The State shall encourage and support financial institutions, other enterprises, institutions and individuals to invest funds to support the development and construction of poverty-stricken areas.
No unit or individual may intercept or misappropriate poverty alleviation funds. Audit authorities shall strengthen the audit and supervision of poverty alleviation funds.

Article 87 The people's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to gradually improve the agricultural administrative management system that meets the requirements of the development of the socialist market economy.
The competent agricultural administrative departments and relevant competent administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen their duties of planning, guidance, management, coordination, supervision and service, conduct administration according to law, and enforce the law impartially.
The competent agricultural administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within the scope of their duties, improve the administrative law enforcement contingent, implement comprehensive law enforcement, and enhance the efficiency and level of law enforcement.

Article 88 When performing their duties of law enforcement supervision and inspection, the competent agricultural administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level and their law enforcement personnel shall have the right to take the following measures:
(1) Requiring the unit or individual under inspection to explain the situation and provide relevant documents, licenses and materials;
(2) Ordering the unit or individual under inspection to cease acts that violate this Law and perform statutory obligations.
When performing their duties of supervision and inspection, the agricultural administrative law enforcement personnel shall present their administrative law enforcement credentials to the unit or individual under inspection and observe law enforcement procedures. The relevant unit or individual shall cooperate with the agricultural administrative law enforcement personnel in performing their duties according to law, and shall not refuse or obstruct them.

Article 89 The competent agricultural administrative departments and agricultural production and operation units must be completely separated in terms of institutions, personnel and finance. The competent agricultural administrative departments and their staff members shall not participate in or engage in agricultural production and operation activities.

Article 90 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of this Law, infringes upon the property rights such as the right to land contractual management or other lawful rights and interests of farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations shall cease the infringement and restore the original state; if losses or damages are caused, they shall bear compensation liability according to law.
If a state functionary, by taking advantage of his position or in any other name, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations, he shall compensate for the losses and shall be given administrative sanctions by the unit to which he belongs or by the competent superior authority.
Article 91 Whoever violates the provisions of Articles 19, 25, 62 and 71 of this Law shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws or administrative regulations.

Article 93 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Article 67 of this Law, illegally collects fees, imposes fines or makes apportionments on farmers or agricultural production and operation organizations shall be stopped by the competent superior authority, which shall also make an announcement; if money has already been collected or manpower or material resources have already been used, the competent superior authority shall order the return of the money already collected within a time limit or the compensation for the manpower and material resources already used at a discounted price, and the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given administrative sanctions by the competent superior authority or the unit to which they belong; if the circumstances are serious enough to constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 95 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 73 of this Law, compels farmers to make financial contributions in lieu of labor shall be ordered by the people's government of the township (town) to make corrections and return the illegally collected funds.

Article 96 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Article 74 of this Law, compels farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations to accept paid services shall be ordered by the relevant people's government to make corrections and return the illegally collected fees; if the circumstances are serious, the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given administrative sanctions; if losses are caused to farmers and agricultural production and operation organizations, compensation liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 97 If a staff member of the competent agricultural administrative department of a people's government at or above the county level, in violation of the provisions of this Law, participates in or engages in agricultural production and operation activities, he shall be given administrative sanctions according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 98 The provisions of this Law concerning farmers shall apply to the employees of state-owned farms, pastures, forest farms, fisheries and other enterprises and institutions who undertake contracted management.
Article 99 This Law shall come into force as of March 1, 2003.
